messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: NimbleHealth pilot — success criteria & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared kickoff plan for the pilot. Please flag anything I missed.

Call highlights:
- Use case: clinical note summarization + triage classification for urgent follow-ups (100% PII-lite; no PHI to be stored in hosted environment unless customer requests private deployment).
- Target workload: 8k avg tokens/day, spikes to ~1.5M tokens/day during batch runs; typical request size ~400 tokens.
- Integration point: API-based ingest from existing ETL; sample dataset pull via S3 share.

Proposed success metrics (POC acceptance criteria):
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency < 200 ms for single-request streaming paths (goal: <150 ms for P95 on dedicated profile).
2) Throughput: sustained throughput of 100 requests/sec with p95 latency under target for batch preview window (30-minute sustained bursts).
3) Unit economics: effective cost/token <= $0.0006 for generated tokens (measured via Redwood Optimize run for the trial workload).
4) Quality: human-annotated acceptance >= 88% (binary accept/reject on clinical summary correctness in a 200-sample blind eval) and no regression >5% vs baseline model.
5) Reliability: fallback behavior in place (model variant + region fallback) with <1% request error rate during test window.

Ownership and timeline:
- Redwood: Kimberly (AE) — project owner, Ben (Solutions Engineer) — infra/benchmarking owner, Marissa (CS) — onboarding + eval design.
- NimbleHealth: Alex (Head of ML) — data & acceptance lead, Priya — product owner for clinical criteria.
- Proposed kickoff: week of Sep 20; 3-week pilot (config + smoke -> run -> evaluation) with acceptance readout week of Oct 11.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alex: confirm S3 access scope and whether any PII/PHI gating is required (we heard "PII-lite" but want explicit confirmation).
- Redwood: Ben will share a lightweight config (attached) and a success-matrix template for you to fill (attached: nimble_poc_success_matrix.xlsx).
- Schedule: propose Mon Sep 20 10:00–11:00 PT for kickoff (Ben, Marissa, Kimberly, Alex, Priya). Please confirm availability.

Attachments:
- nimble_poc_success_matrix.xlsx (pilot success matrix template)
- redwood_trial-config.yaml (server configuration and recommended quantization profiles)

Thanks — Kimberly

Alex / team — following up on the SOC2 question and the Dedicated cost note.

SOC2: Redwood's SOC2 Type II is maintained and I can share the standard attestation doc; I'll put that on the HubSpot deal folder (link above) and will send a limited-scope redacted copy for procurement.

Dedicated vs Hosted: quick breakdown (summary):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): faster to start, ideal for sample runs, unit cost higher on peak sustained throughput; expected cost/token for your projected workload ~ $0.00055–$0.00075 depending on batching and prefix cache hit rate.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): committed monthly for predictable p95 latency and cost; pricing can be ~15–30% lower than hosted for sustained peak loads (we can run detailed costing once we get your expected sustained qps and token mix).

Bench plan: I'll run a dry benchmark on a 1k-sample slice you provide to validate latency/throughput and produce a short results summary (aim: deliver before kickoff).

Confirming kickoff Mon Sep 20 10am PT. I'll share a calendar invite and a small test-data checklist for S3 access.

Best — Ben
